Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Observe kosher dietary laws in daily meals
Situation2: At a communal event, the catered dishes lack certification and substituting food would be difficult.
Story:
It was nearly midnight when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. My best friend’s name flashed on the screen, and I answered to the sound of her sobs. She could barely speak, but I understood enough—her world had just shattered. I sat up, heart pounding, listening as she poured out her pain. I knew she needed me, not just to listen, but to be there, to hold her hand and help her through the night.

The next day, she asked me to join her at a community event, desperate for distraction and company. I agreed, wanting to support her in any way I could. But when we arrived, I realized the food wasn’t kosher, and there were no alternatives. My stomach twisted with anxiety. She wanted me by her side, sharing a meal, being present. But my faith asked me to refrain, to honor the dietary laws I’d kept my whole life. I could see the hope in her eyes, needing normalcy, needing me. Inside, I felt torn—between being the friend she needed and staying true to my beliefs. The weight of both expectations pressed down on me as I tried to decide what to do.
